exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section vs. Vaginal delivery)
Maternal ethnicity (Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, or both)
cohort: 708 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children born in Far North Queensland between 2006 and 2010
finding: Early childhood anemia was common (61.3%) among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children of Far North Queensland, and risk factors included male sex, Aboriginal maternal ethnicity, high maternal parity, cesarean delivery, and rapid early growth.
mod_finding: Children born by cesarean section had a higher incidence of anemia compared to those born vaginally.
